title: Integration eines hochintegrierten Quantenempfängers in ein Quantum Key Distribution System mit kontinuierlichen Variablen - QuNET+DECODE (optimized coherent receiver for cv-qkd systems)
abstract: Das Projekt QuNET+DECODE hatte die Entwicklung eines leistungsstarken, vollständig integrierten Quantenempfängers für die Quanten-Schlüsselverteilung mit kontinuierlichen Variablen (CV-QKD) sowie dessen nahtlose Einbindung in die bestehende QuNET-Infrastruktur zum Ziel. Aufbauend auf einer Vielzahl bestehender CV-QKD-Experimente, die sich durch vielfältige Modulationsformate und Homodyn-Detektionsverfahren auszeichnen, verfolgte das Konsortium folgende Ziele: (i) die Anforderungen an das optische Frontend und den Transimpedanzverstärker (TIA) für ein dualpolarisationsoptimiertes CV-QKD-Protokoll zu definieren, (ii) die Empfänger-Schnittstellen mit dem QuNET-CV-QKD-System zu validieren und (iii) Codierungen höherer Ordnung im Stokes-Raum für die polarisationsdiverse Schlüsselgenerierung zu untersuchen. Zu Projektanfang wurden detaillierte Empfängerspezifikationen (Spannungsversorgung, Datenüberwachungsschnittstelle, Platzbedarf, elektromagnetische Suszeptibilität) festgelegt und Schnittstellentests mit kommerziellen Detektoren durchgeführt. Spektrale Rauschmessungen zeigten einen linearen Rauschpegel und ein geeignetes Verhältnis von Quanten- zu klassischem Rauschen. In anschließenden Experimenten mit einem polarisationsdiversen 90°-Hybrid sowohl in Glasfaser- als auch in Freistrahlverbindungen wurden Polarisationsdrift, Übersprechen und die Auswirkungen paralleler DWDM-Kanäle charakterisiert, wobei die für den integrierten DECODE-Empfänger erwarteten Bedingungen nachgebildet wurden. Das im Rahmen des Projekts entwickelte integrierte Modul wies eine unzureichende Trennung zwischen Quanten- und elektronischem Rauschen auf, was seinen Einsatz im QuNET-Schlüsselversuch (SE4) ausschloss. Dies unterstreicht die Notwendigkeit einer weiteren Optimierung des Rauschverhaltens integrierter Detektoren in Folgeuntersuchungen. Auf theoretischer Ebene untersuchte das Projekt Terme höherer Ordnung bei der Kodierung im Stokes-Raum und fand dabei hybride Kommutationsrelationen, die neue Forschungsrichtungen zur Quanteninformationsverarbeitung mit Polarisationszuständen eröffnen könnten.

title: FORMING A BUBBLE IN THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE MARKET
abstract: The dynamics of the development of the artificial intelligence market has been studied, highlighting not only financial indicators, but also research and social activity. The dynamics of investments in the AI market has been analyzed. It has been established that in recent years there has been a rapid development of the artificial intelligence market. It is artificial intelligence that is becoming the main means of technological and economic development, in various areas, such as business, finance, medicine. artificial intelligence in these areas entails significant investments, due to the high level of expectations, regarding the future impact on the development of the world economy. However, along with the active development of technology, there is also an increase in fears and discussions about the possible formation of an economic bubble in the artificial intelligence market. It is substantiated that if we characterize the AI market, it is worth noting the growth in the value of technology companies, rapid and large-scale venture investments, and the constant emergence of new startups. All of this bears some resemblance to previous tech booms, as well as the dot-com bubble. The capital expenditures of companies for financing artificial intelligence and the dynamics of financing artificial intelligence infrastructure are estimated. An analysis of general trends in large investments in new technologies and AI is performed. Examples of economic bubbles in the AI market are given. A comparison of previous bubbles and the modern AI market is carried out, common characteristics and differences are highlighted. Problems and risks of the development of the AI market are indicated. In the process of research, methods of comparative analysis, generalization of scientific approaches, as well as research of modern trends in the development of the technology sector were used, analysis of international economic data and reports, as well as research of modern literature on economic and technological bubbles.

title: RouteGraph-Mona: Confusion-Aware Routing Fine-Tuning for Mineral Image Classification
abstract: Mineral image classification is important for geological exploration and resource development, but it remains challenging due to substantial intra-class variations in appearance and high inter-class visual similarity. Multi-cognitive Visual Adapter (Mona) is a vision-oriented parameter-efficient adapter that adapts pre-trained visual models by tuning only a few parameters. However, Mona statically aggregates responses from multiple scales, limiting its ability to accommodate sample-specific scale preferences and model confusion among visually similar mineral categories. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{RouteGraph-Mona}, a lightweight route-space regularization method built on Mona. Specifically, we replace Mona's static multi-scale aggregation with sample-adaptive routing. The resulting branch-selection behavior defines a compact routing space that captures each image's scale preferences. We then regularize the resulting routing signatures with class-wise route anchors and confusion-weighted margins. The route anchors encourage class-consistent routing patterns, while the margins promote greater separation between visually similar categories in the routing space. Experiments on three public mineral image datasets with two visual backbones show that RouteGraph-Mona consistently outperforms Mona in mean accuracy and remains competitive with representative fine-tuning methods and mineral image classification baselines.

title: APEx: Distillation of Agent Procedural Experience for Adaptive Deep Research Question Answering
abstract: Deep research agents augment large language models with external tools to answer complex, long-horizon questions through multi-turn reasoning. Learning from prior experience is crucial for continual improvement, yet existing methods either retrieve verbose task-specific traces that burden decision-making, or distill procedural skills that remain decoupled from downstream policy adaptation. We propose APEx, a hierarchical experience utilization framework that organizes interaction history into instance-level trajectory memories and category-level procedural skills, and couples them through a closed-loop architecture of Executor, Distiller, and Planner. The three modules are optimized via a three-stage alternating GRPO training paradigm, enabling reward-guided skill distillation rather than fixed-prompt generation. At test time, distilled skills serve as procedural priors for online Planner adaptation through skill-guided test-time reinforcement learning, allowing ground-truth-free self-improvement with skill-alignment regularization to prevent policy drift. Experiments on 7 benchmarks demonstrate that APEx achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing GPT-5.4 by 14.7 points and the strongest memory-augmented baseline by 3.0 points.

title: Graph-MambaNav: Spatial-Temporal Graph Mamba Leveraging Object-Relation Knowledge for Object-Goal Navigation
abstract: Object-goal navigation requires an agent to reason over object relationships and prioritize target-relevant objects for efficient decision making in unseen environments. While existing graph-based methods incorporate target-awareness at the feature or attention level, they remain permutation-invariant and lack an explicit mechanism to control information propagation order, limiting their ability to model target-dependent importance and long-range dependencies. In contrast, Graph-Mamba highlights that node prioritization through sequence ordering is critical for effective global reasoning. In this work, we investigate the node prioritization mechanism in Graph-Mamba and study its role in object navigation. We propose Graph-MambaNav, a target-aware spatial-temporal graph encoding framework that introduces a heuristic ordering over objects based on their relevance to the target, allowing more informative objects to be processed later to aggregate richer context. Both node ordering and edge weights are initialized from LLM-derived commonsense object relationships, providing a unified prior for structured reasoning. A spatial module integrates local message passing with global GraphMamba-based selective scanning, while a temporal module applies Mamba-based sequence modeling over object-wise temporal orders, allowing selective aggregation of historical context for long-range temporal reasoning. Experiments on AI2-THOR and RoboTHOR demonstrate improved navigation performance with generalization, and additional real-world robot deployment further validates the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

title: TaLK: Text-attributed Graph Dataset Distillation via Coupling Language Model with Graph-Aware Kernel
abstract: Text-attributed graphs (TAGs) are widely used in many real-world domains, and learning on TAGs requires jointly modeling text semantics and graph structure. A standard approach for modeling TAGs is to combine a language model (LM) and a graph neural network (GNN), but joint training is computationally expensive and difficult to scale. Dataset distillation is a promising way to reduce training costs, but existing methods are not well suited to TAGs because they are typically designed for a single modality or still require repeatedly training expensive LM-GNN models on the full dataset during distillation. To address this, we propose TaLK, an effective dataset distillation method for TAGs that couples an LM with a graph-aware neural tangent kernel. This design enables efficient dataset distillation, avoiding repeated joint training on the full dataset while reflecting both textual and structural information for effective TAG learning. Experiments on multiple TAG benchmarks show that TaLK consistently outperforms existing baselines and achieves up to 97% of full-dataset performance with only 1% synthetic data.

title: PREDICTIVE AI FOR PERSONALIZED SECOND LANGUAGE LEARNING: DEVELOPING A DIGITAL MODEL TO PREDICT LEARNER DIFFICULTIES AND OPTIMIZE LANGUAGE INSTRUCTION
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), learning analytics, and adaptive educational technologies has created new opportunities for personalized second language (L2) learning. Traditional language instruction often relies on standardized curricula and periodic assessments, which may not adequately identify individual learners’ difficulties before they become persistent. Predictive artificial intelligence (Predictive AI) enables the analysis of learner-generated data, the identification of patterns associated with learning difficulties, the prediction of potential learning problems, and the recommendation of appropriate instructional interventions. This study aims to develop a conceptual digital model for Predictive AI-supported personalized second language learning. A conceptual-analytical research design was employed, involving the analysis and synthesis of recent studies on artificial intelligence in language education, adaptive learning, learning analytics, intelligent tutoring systems, learner profiling, personalized instruction, and self-regulated learning. The analysis indicates that AI-supported language learning can provide individualized feedback, adaptive learning pathways, diagnostic assessment, and personalized learning resources. However, existing research has placed greater emphasis on automated feedback and intelligent tutoring systems than on predictive learner profiling and the early identification of learning difficulties. Based on these findings, the study proposes the Predictive AI Personalized Language Learning Model (PAI-PLL Model), which comprises six interconnected stages: learner data collection, learner profiling, difficulty prediction, personalized recommendation, adaptive instruction, and continuous monitoring. The model integrates linguistic, behavioral, performance-based, and learning-process indicators while emphasizing teacher oversight and the ethical use of data. The proposed model conceptualizes Predictive AI as a decision-support mechanism rather than an autonomous replacement for teachers. Its principal contribution lies in integrating predictive analytics and personalized L2 instruction into a continuous preventive learning cycle. The model provides a theoretical and methodological foundation for future empirical research aimed at developing intelligent language-learning environments capable of identifying learner difficulties at an early stage and optimizing instructional decision-making.

evidence.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), learning analytics, and adaptive educational technologies has created new opportunities for personalized second language (L2) learning. Traditional language instruction often relies on standardized curricula and periodic assessments, which may not adequately identify individual learners’ difficulties before they become persistent. Predictive artificial intelligence (Predictive AI) enables the analysis of learner-generated data, the identification of patterns associated with learning difficulties, the prediction of potential learning problems, and the recommendation of appropriate instructional interventions. This study aims to develop a conceptual digital model for Predictive AI-supported personalized second language learning. A conceptual-analytical research design was employed, involving the analysis and synthesis of recent studies on artificial intelligence in language education, adaptive learning, learning analytics, intelligent tutoring systems, learner profiling, personalized instruction, and self-regulated learning. The analysis indicates that AI-supported language learning can provide individualized feedback, adaptive learning pathways, diagnostic assessment, and personalized learning resources. However, existing research has placed greater emphasis on automated feedback and intelligent tutoring systems than on predictive learner profiling and the early identification of learning difficulties. Based on these findings, the study proposes the Predictive AI Personalized Language Learning Model (PAI-PLL Model), which comprises six interconnected stages: learner data collection, learner profiling, difficulty prediction, personalized recommendation, adaptive instruction, and continuous monitoring. The model integrates linguistic, behavioral, performance-based, and learning-process indicators while emphasizing teacher oversight and the ethical use of data. The proposed model conceptualizes Predictive AI as a decision-support mechanism rather than an autonomous replacement for teachers. Its principal contribution lies in integrating predictive analytics and personalized L2 instruction into a continuous preventive learning cycle. The model provides a theoretical and methodological foundation for future empirical research aimed at developing intelligent language-learning environments capable of identifying learner difficulties at an early stage and optimizing instructional decision-making.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Design with Dynamic Resource Allocation
abstract: Quantum circuit design presents a significant challenge in the field of quantum computing, demanding efficient and robust circuit layouts. Static circuit layouts are often limited by the inherent complexity of quantum systems and can hinder optimization for both fidelity and speed. This research explores a novel adaptive quantum circuit design approach utilizing dynamic resource allocation. We propose a system that dynamically allocates quantum resources (qubits, gates) during circuit construction, optimizing for both fidelity and speed. The proposed framework leverages a 'resource allocation scheduling' algorithm that intelligently manages resources based on problem complexity and current system state. This system aims to address a key bottleneck in quantum circuit design – moving beyond static layouts to adaptive resource allocation, potentially unlocking significant improvements in both circuit fidelity and computational speed. This work presents a complete theoretical and practical implementation of this approach, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulation and preliminary experimentation. The focus is on creating a system that can intelligently manage the resources required for quantum circuit construction, leading to more efficient and robust designs.

title: Title: Algorithmic Complexity of Cognitive Networks via Quantum Simulation
abstract: Cognitive networks, mimicking the human brain, exhibit complex interactions and emergent behaviors. Traditional complexity measures, while useful, often fail to adequately represent the subtle quantum-influenced processes underpinning reasoning and learning. This paper investigates the algorithmic complexity of cognitive networks through a novel quantum simulation approach, aiming to quantify and potentially enhance the network's inherent complexity. We propose a quantum algorithm designed to explore the potential state space of the network, revealing underlying quantum-enhanced reasoning pathways. The research seeks to provide a deeper, more nuanced understanding of cognitive systems by utilizing the principles of quantum mechanics. This work addresses a critical gap in our understanding of how quantum phenomena might influence network dynamics.

title: Dynamic Topology for Quantum Information Encoding and Puzzle Solving
abstract: Dynamic topology, a fascinating field of mathematics, offers a novel approach to quantum information processing. This paper explores the potential of dynamically evolving topological structures to enhance quantum information encoding and puzzle-solving capabilities. We investigate a specific algorithm leveraging dynamic topology to generate and manipulate quantum states, fostering a novel approach to quantum computation. The core mechanism involves the application of dynamic topology to create entangled states with enhanced properties, ultimately leading to more efficient and secure quantum computation. The research focuses on a particular quantum puzzle – a variation of the game of Nim – where dynamic topology facilitates the development of complex, unpredictable patterns. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in generating intricate puzzle solutions, showcasing a significant advancement in quantum algorithm design. This work represents a significant step toward harnessing the inherent properties of dynamic topology for advanced quantum technologies.

title: Quantum-Guided Optimization for Non-Linear Systems
abstract: Quantum-Guided Optimization (QGO) represents a novel approach to solving complex optimization problems, particularly those exhibiting non-linear characteristics. This paper introduces a framework for optimizing non-linear systems utilizing quantum entanglement, aiming to significantly accelerate and enhance traditional optimization techniques. We detail the core mechanism of QGO, outlining its architecture, quantum algorithm, and potential benefits in terms of computational efficiency and solution quality. The proposed method leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to facilitate the exploration of the solution space and guide the optimization process towards optimal configurations. The paper provides a comprehensive discussion of the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of QGO.

title: Probabilistic Verification of Concurrent Programs with Abstract Interpretation
abstract: Concurrent program verification remains a significant challenge due to the inherent complexities arising from interactions between multiple processes. Traditional static analysis techniques, including abstract interpretation, often struggle to capture the full range of possible concurrent behaviors, leading to false negatives—verifying programs that actually exhibit undesirable behavior. This paper proposes a novel approach that combines abstract interpretation with probabilistic models to provide a more rigorous verification framework. We introduce an extension to abstract interpretation that incorporates probabilistic representations of concurrent execution, allowing us to quantify and reason about uncertainties in synchronization and communication. The core idea is to represent program states not as single values but as probability distributions, reflecting the likelihood of different execution paths. This approach significantly improves the ability to detect subtle concurrency errors that would otherwise be missed by deterministic abstract interpretation. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this method through a detailed theoretical analysis and illustrate its application with a simplified example. The key contribution lies in the formal integration of probabilistic models into the abstract interpretation process, offering a more nuanced and accurate representation of concurrent program behavior. ---

title: Quantum Phase Field Simulation: Adaptive Optimization for Enhanced Simulation
abstract: Quantum phase field (QPF) simulations offer a powerful tool for studying complex quantum systems, particularly in areas such as condensed matter physics and quantum materials. However, traditional QPF simulations often require extensive parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and limit the exploration of the parameter space. This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization algorithm for QPF simulations, designed to automatically adjust simulation parameters based on the resulting data, thereby significantly improving simulation accuracy and efficiency. The algorithm leverages the inherent dynamics of quantum phase field simulations to dynamically adjust parameters, ensuring a robust and efficient simulation process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to achieve superior results compared to existing optimization techniques.

title: Bayesian Networks for High-Dimensional Data Anomaly Detection Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for high-dimensional data anomaly detection leveraging Bayesian Networks (BNs). The core idea is to represent complex, high-dimensional data as a BN, enabling probabilistic inference to identify anomalies based on deviations from learned dependencies. This approach offers advantages over traditional methods by explicitly modeling relationships between variables and providing interpretable anomaly explanations. The framework utilizes probability distributions to determine the likelihood of data points belonging to normal patterns, and then performs causal analysis to identify the root causes of anomalies. We explore the application of BNs for anomaly detection, demonstrating their ability to handle intricate data dependencies and provide insights into the underlying reasons for anomalous behavior. The framework's key contributions lie in its ability to effectively model high-dimensional data and offer a transparent and explainable approach to anomaly detection.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum simulation, focusing on the development of a method for modeling quantum simulation based on topological structure. The core claim is that this method will generate more efficient simulations and reveal complex structures within quantum systems. Traditional quantum simulation often relies on classical methods, limiting our ability to capture the intricate structure of quantum systems. Topology modeling offers a unique avenue for simulating these structures directly, reducing simulation errors and significantly enhancing simulation accuracy. This work explores the design of a computational framework predicated on topological structure, aiming to minimize error and improve simulation fidelity. We present a foundational mechanism involving the inherent properties of topological structures, leading to a more precise and efficient simulation process. The resulting system will be capable of generating more accurate and insightful visualizations of quantum system behavior.

title: 基于量子噪声的量子密钥分发协议
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging the inherent characteristics of quantum noise. The core claim is that exploiting quantum noise can significantly enhance the security of QKD. The proposed protocol utilizes the random nature of quantum noise to introduce disturbances for eavesdropping attempts, ultimately improving key distribution security. The protocol's design focuses on mitigating the impact of channel noise while maintaining key rate. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outline the key components of the system. The protocol's effectiveness is analyzed through mathematical modeling, demonstrating its potential for robust key exchange in noisy environments. The analysis highlights the trade-offs between key rate and security, a crucial consideration in practical QKD implementations.

title: Homomorphic Encryption for Privacy-Preserving Data Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the application of homomorphic encryption (HE) to enable privacy-preserving data analysis. Traditional methods of data analysis frequently necessitate decryption, introducing significant security vulnerabilities. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing HE to perform computations directly on encrypted data, effectively shielding the underlying data from exposure. The core claim is that HE allows for secure data analysis without decryption. The mechanism involves constructing a homomorphic encryption computing environment, employing HE algorithms for encryption and operations, ultimately facilitating safe analysis of sensitive data. This work investigates the feasibility and potential benefits of this approach, addressing the critical need for robust data privacy in increasingly data-driven environments. The primary contribution lies in demonstrating a practical framework for utilizing HE in data analysis scenarios, moving beyond theoretical concepts toward tangible security solutions. ---

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Adaptive Parameter Scaffolding
abstract: Training deep neural networks is often hampered by the accumulation of errors, leading to suboptimal performance and instability. This paper introduces a novel architecture, Adaptive Parameter Scaffolding (APS), designed to mitigate this problem through an intrinsic self-correcting mechanism. The core idea is to integrate a dynamically adjusting "scaffolding" network alongside the primary neural network. This scaffolding network continuously monitors the primary network's output and internal activations, identifying potential error signals and proactively adjusting the weights of the primary network to minimize these errors. The adjustment process is governed by a feedback loop, creating a self-correcting system. We present a theoretical framework for understanding the dynamics of this system, outlining key equations and mathematical relationships. The design emphasizes adaptability and real-time error correction, potentially leading to more robust and efficient training processes for deep neural networks. The proposed approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm compared to traditional training methods, shifting from passive adjustment to active error correction within the network itself.

title: Formal Specification and Verification of Quantum Computing Algorithms
abstract: The verification of quantum computing algorithms presents a significant hurdle due to the probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics and the complex entanglement inherent in quantum computations. This paper proposes a novel approach to address this challenge by developing a formal language and a corresponding verification tool tailored explicitly for quantum algorithm specification and verification. The system leverages concepts from quantum information theory and formal methods to provide a rigorous framework for ensuring the correctness of quantum algorithms. We introduce a new formalism that allows for precise description of quantum circuits and their operations, combined with automated theorem proving techniques to systematically verify the algorithm's behavior against a given specification. The key innovation lies in the ability to reason about quantum states and measurements within a formal setting, enabling a more comprehensive understanding and validation of these algorithms. This work lays the foundation for increased confidence in the development and deployment of quantum computing technologies.

title: A Low-Resource Arabic Dataset and Transformer-Based Benchmark for Dark Pattern Detection in E-Commerce Mobile Applications
abstract: Arabic remains underrepresented in many task-specific natural language processing (NLP) resources and benchmarks, particularly for specialized user interface (UI) understanding tasks. In mobile commerce, Arabic UI text may contain persuasive or deceptive design cues known as dark patterns; however, Arabic-language dark pattern detection remains largely unexplored. To the best of our knowledge, this paper presents the first ML-based benchmark for Arabic dark pattern detection. We construct a novel annotated dataset of 223 Arabic UI text strings from nine e-commerce mobile applications operating in Saudi Arabia, labeled across five dark pattern categories and a non-dark-pattern class (Cohen’s kappa κ = 0.89). Using a stratified, leakage-free 70/10/20 split with parent-aware paraphrase augmentation applied only to the training partition, we fine-tune five pretrained transformer models: AraBERTv2, MARBERT, mBERT, BERT-base-uncased, and RoBERTa-base. Our primary evaluation is 5-fold cross-validation on the 223 original, non-augmented instances, separate from the augmented training corpus used for the held-out test comparison. Under this evaluation, MARBERT achieves the strongest performance (mean macro-F1 = 0.4230), numerically ahead of AraBERTv2 (0.2998) by a margin that does not reach statistical significance at five folds (p ≈ 0.064), and ahead of mBERT (0.3234); MARBERT significantly outperforms both English-only baselines, and mBERT is numerically stronger than both, though mBERT was not directly tested against them for significance. This suggests pre-training on dialectal, code-switched Arabic may matter more here than Arabic pre-training alone. Per-class analysis shows every model struggles with several minority categories, indicating Arabic dark pattern detection remains genuinely difficult at current data volumes. The annotated dataset is publicly released to support future low-resource Arabic NLP research.

title: Rethinking the Teacher-Student Framework for Test-Time Adaptation
abstract: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) has recently emerged as a promising strategy that allows the adaptation of pre-trained models to changing data distributions at deployment time, without access to any labels. To mitigate error accumulation, researchers have widely adopted the teacher-student framework, though its long-term stability is often taken for granted. In this work, we challenge the common strategy of setting the teacher weights to an exponential moving average of the student by showing that error accumulation still occurs, although it is mostly apparent on longer sequences compared to those commonly utilized. Finally, we show that those changes can be seamlessly and effectively applied to various architectures and experimental setups, including semantic segmentation. title: VTOS: Learning to Orchestrate Vision Tools by Co-Searching Solutions and Observers
abstract: Vision foundation tools such as open-vocabulary detectors, segmentation models, and post-processing operators are powerful building blocks for computer vision, but their effectiveness depends heavily on how they are orchestrated: which tools are used, in what order, with what parameters, and under what visual conditions. Existing visual-programming agents typically generate a fixed solution pipeline, making them brittle under dense objects, occlusion, small targets, and domain shift. We introduce VTOS (Vision Tools Orchestration Search), a framework for adaptive visual tool orchestration through joint solution-observer search. VTOS co-searches executable solution programs that compose vision tools such as Grounding DINO, SAM, NMS, and slice-and-detect, together with observer programs that diagnose candidate solutions, identify failure modes, and generate actionable feedback. These observations are accumulated in a shared VisionThoughts knowledge base to guide subsequent search. We evaluate VTOS through two case studies: dense object counting on LVIS-Count and zero-shot plant-disease segmentation on PlantSeg-OOD, which stress different orchestration challenges including threshold calibration, NMS, slicing, mask refinement, and domain generalization. Across both tasks, VTOS outperforms static tool pipelines and agentic visual-programming baselines, specifically in complex settings such as dense, occluded scenes and out-of-distribution segmentation where static pipelines leave measurable headroom, rather than in standard tasks where a single well-calibrated tool already approaches its ceiling.

title: SecureMed-FL: A Privacy- and Security-Aware Federated Learning Framework for Brain Tumor MRI Classification
abstract: SecureMed-FL is a privacy- and security-aware federated learning framework for brain tumor MRI classification across five simulated healthcare institutions. The framework integrates FedAvg and FedProx optimization, controlled non-IID heterogeneity, record-level differential privacy, black-box membership-inference auditing, and masking-based secure-aggregation simulation within a unified experimental pipeline. The study evaluates the trade-offs among predictive utility, heterogeneity robustness, privacy protection, empirical leakage, and aggregation efficiency in trustworthy federated medical imaging.

title: ZenBrain: Neuroscience-Inspired Agent Memory Library for LLM Agents
abstract: Source code release of ZenBrain, an open-source agent memory library for LLM agents: seven neuroscience-inspired memory layers (working, short-term, episodic, semantic, procedural, core, cross-context) behind a memory coordinator that stores, recalls, forgets and consolidates, and a library of 20 algorithm modules (10 core algorithms + 10 advanced research modules) such as FSRS spaced repetition, Hebbian learning and sleep replay. Which mechanisms the coordinator runs on its own and which the library offers as functions is listed in the repository README. TypeScript, Apache-2.0; the algorithm package has zero runtime dependencies. 822 automated tests, CI on Node 22, 24 and 26 and against PostgreSQL with pgvector. This record pins the exact released version: Git tag v0.5.1 (commit 12d9076f) Source archive in this record: zenbrain-v0.5.1.tar.gz, SHA-256 a65a6f59728a54c98a9646990be5d97d63730d94c545215c478599b08854a503 npm: @zensation/algorithms@0.5.1 — dist SHA-1 bc4ccce27d9c3117c872c0fe9b43ef91de2aa6d3, 153 files; @zensation/core@0.5.1 and @zensation/mcp@0.2.1 from the same tag Relation to the paper (arXiv:2604.23878): the architecture described there comprises 15 neuroscience-inspired mechanisms — 9 foundational algorithms plus 6 Predictive Memory Architecture (PMA) components. The 6 PMA components are proprietary and run in the production system; this open-source package ships the algorithm library (20 modules). The two counts describe different things and are both stated in the paper and the repository README.

title: Cohesion of an Evolving Text
abstract: A diary of one hundred entries written by a language model carries recurring themes, found after the fact as sets of sparse-autoencoder features that fire together within a bounded stretch of entries. We ask what a witness could have seen at each point of the diary's life, and build the instrument that answers: the same detector run on the log up to each entry τ, with nothing carried between prefixes. Three objects result. A theme becomes a chain of complexes linked across τ by shared features, with a cohesion, the fraction the link carries, and a gap, what it gains and loses. The base is the largest complex at τ: the flagged mass the log cannot yet tell apart in time. The ground is the set of features on in most entries, which the detector excludes by construction. On the first diary the base forms over the first forty entries, holds, and from entry sixty-five articulates into themes; a theme becomes witnessable only after the text has left it, so every theme has a target-time and a later witness-time. Four diaries written under the same protocol share the shape of this process and share a ground of 6,182 features, while their bases share almost nothing. One feature, firing on the coupling of machine and human described as living tissue, has a career in all four in four different figures. The chains, the base and the ground supply a decidable Semantic Witness Log in the sense of dynamic open homotopy type theory: each link is a witness record with target-time and witness-time, cohesion is Presence, the bounded gap is Generativity, the unlinked flash is scatter, the ended chain is rupture, the re-linked chain is resurrection. We state a small calculus for the instrument in that form and close with the design, not yet run, for the same instrument over parallel lives sampled from one prefix. Full HTML text: https://icra.tanazur.org/papers/cohesion-of-an-evolving-text/ — ICRA pre-print series: https://icra.tanazur.org/

title: ST-T1024: The Sovereign Bridge Between Quantum Cryptography and Fintech Security — A Position Paper on Deterministic Hardware as the Foundation for Post-Quantum Financial Infrastructure
abstract: The launch of X Money in July 2026—a payments service offering digital wallets,peer-to-peer transfers, and a Visa debit card with up to 6% APY—has been immediatelyfollowed by a wave of targeted attacks against user accounts. Simultaneously, the quantum computing threat looms: NIST has finalized post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards(FIPS 203-205), yet the financial industry struggles to implement them within the tightmemory and energy budgets of embedded and mobile devices. This paper argues that ST-T1024—an open standard for deterministic, ultra-low-power,sovereign AI inference—provides the unified hardware foundation that solves both problems. We demonstrate that:1. ST-T1024 makes it easy to design quantum cryptography algorithms by providing ageneral-purpose deterministic computing platform with ternary logic, formal verification, and provable timing guarantees.2. ST-T1024 makes it easy to implement any NIST-standardized PQC algorithm through itsdomain-tile architecture, 75% ROM / 25% SRAM split, and SK-1024 sovereign updateprotocol.3. X Money's security challenges—password reset attacks, phishing campaigns, and thelooming quantum threat—are directly addressable by deploying ST-T1024 as the secure enclave for every X Money transaction. The diagnosis is complete. The cure is ready. The path is clear.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithm for Parallel Wavefront Optimization
abstract: Quantum-inspired algorithms represent a promising avenue for enhancing the performance of parallel waveffront optimization, a crucial task in various computational fields. Standard parallel waveffront algorithms, while effective, often face challenges with increasing computational complexity, limiting their scalability. This paper introduces a novel quantum-inspired algorithm that leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to efficiently explore the solution space, aiming to overcome these limitations. The algorithm's design centers around mimicking the principles of quantum wavefunctions, offering a potential pathway to substantial improvements in optimization speed and accuracy. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's core mechanics, its mathematical formulation, and its potential benefits within the context of parallel waveffront optimization. The research focuses on demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and preliminary analysis, highlighting its potential to address the scalability issues inherent in traditional approaches.

title: Title: Bayesian Variational Quantum Error Mitigation with Adaptive Kernel Selection (BVQ-AKS)
abstract: Quantum computation promises unprecedented computational power, but inherent quantum errors pose a significant barrier to widespread adoption. Variational Quantum Error Mitigation (VQEM) is a crucial technique for reducing these errors, but its effectiveness is heavily dependent on the specific error profile of the quantum circuit. Traditional VQEM methods often rely on a fixed kernel, failing to adequately address the diverse error characteristics across different quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel Bayesian Variational Quantum Error Mitigation (BVQ-AKS) strategy that dynamically adapts the kernel selection process based on the circuit's error profile. The algorithm learns an optimal kernel for each circuit type, enhancing mitigation effectiveness across a broader range of errors. This approach offers a tailored and adaptive method to address the challenges of VQEM, paving the way for more robust and reliable quantum computations.

title: A Universal Computation Architecture Based on Consciousness
abstract: This paper proposes a novel universal computation architecture predicated on the principles of human consciousness. The core argument is that by explicitly modelling the fundamental mechanisms underlying human awareness – perception, integration, and decision-making – we can unlock computational capabilities exceeding those afforded by conventional approaches. This architecture, termed the "Conscious Computation Framework" (CCF), aims to move beyond the limitations of traditional algorithms by incorporating dynamic, context-aware processing, mirroring the adaptive and flexible nature of the human mind. The framework utilizes a multi-layered approach, encompassing sensory input processing, internal model construction, and generative processes. We define key mathematical formalisms for representing these processes, including probabilistic models, Bayesian networks, and dynamical systems. The potential of this approach to enhance reasoning, creativity, and problem-solving is explored, laying the groundwork for a fundamentally new paradigm in artificial intelligence.

title: Quantum Entangled Adaptive Algorithm for Enhanced Efficiency and Robustness
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive algorithm based on quantum entanglement, designed to significantly enhance the efficiency and robustness of computations. Traditional algorithms often struggle with the inherent limitations of classical systems, particularly in scenarios demanding precise and reliable results. This work explores the utilization of quantum entanglement as a key mechanism to overcome these limitations. The algorithm leverages entangled states to enable parallel processing, minimize errors, and achieve a higher degree of accuracy. We detail the core principles of the algorithm, the mathematical foundations underpinning its operation, and the potential benefits in terms of computational speed and stability. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for research in this area.

title: Title: Adaptive Computational Complexity
abstract: This paper explores the concept of adaptive computational complexity, a novel approach to algorithm design that dynamically adjusts the complexity of computations based on the characteristics of the input data. Traditional algorithms often operate with a fixed complexity, regardless of the data's nature. This work proposes a method to dynamically measure and adjust algorithm parameters, optimizing for both accuracy and computational efficiency. The core mechanism involves the implementation of a 'complexity metric' that evaluates the effort required to execute a computation, and subsequently adjusts algorithm parameters to minimize this effort while maintaining acceptable accuracy. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a simplified example, highlighting potential benefits in scenarios with variable input data. The core claim is that this method represents a significant advancement in algorithm design, moving beyond static approaches to a system capable of adapting to data-dependent complexities.

title: Algorithmic Self-Similarity for Network Embedding
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithmic self-similarity approach to network embedding, aiming to optimize the representation of network structure and relationships. The core concept centers on a "self-similar graph" algorithm, which iteratively refines the embedding by capturing emergent patterns. The design addresses a persistent challenge in graph embedding – the difficulty of effectively representing complex network dynamics. We present a novel algorithm that achieves a balance between preserving structural information and capturing meaningful relationships through this self-similar process. The resulting embeddings will exhibit enhanced robustness and potential for downstream applications.

title: Based on Information Bottleneck: A Neural System Model and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to artificial intelligence (AI) based on the information bottleneck (IB) principle, arguing that the fundamental nature of neural system learning lies in identifying and exploiting information bottlenecks. We introduce a computational model designed to mimic the formation and elimination of information bottlenecks within a neural system. This model leverages the core IB theory, aiming to achieve AI learning and reasoning by actively seeking and resolving these bottlenecks. The model's architecture emphasizes the dynamic adjustment of representations to minimize information loss while retaining only the most relevant features for a given task. We present a mathematical framework for describing this process, focusing on variational inference and Kullback-Leibler divergence. The primary contribution of this work is a practical, computationally tractable method for implementing the IB principle in AI, offering a potential pathway towards more efficient and robust learning algorithms. Furthermore, this model's design provides a theoretical basis for understanding how biological neural systems achieve their remarkable learning capabilities. ---

title: Bayesian Optimization for Hyperparameter Tuning of Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, yet its training process is notoriously sensitive to hyperparameter settings. Traditional methods of hyperparameter tuning, such as grid search and random search, are computationally expensive and often inefficient. This paper proposes the application of Bayesian optimization to the hyperparameter tuning of DRL agents. Bayesian optimization leverages a probabilistic model to guide the search process, effectively balancing exploration and exploitation to identify optimal configurations. The core claim is that this approach significantly accelerates the learning process and improves the performance of DRL agents. We detail the implementation of a Bayesian optimization algorithm, focusing on its ability to efficiently navigate the complex hyperparameter space. The results presented demonstrate the efficacy of this method compared to conventional tuning strategies.

title: Algorithmic Complexity Theory for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of future quantum computing, addressing the fragility of quantum information. Current error correction schemes, while effective, suffer from significant computational overhead, limiting the scalability of quantum devices. This paper explores the application of algorithmic complexity theory to design a novel complexity class and algorithm for QEC, specifically targeting near-term error correction. We introduce a new complexity measure that directly quantifies the 'complexity' of the error correction process, linking it to the underlying quantum system's dynamics. This approach aims to significantly reduce computational burden compared to existing methods, potentially unlocking practical quantum computing. The theoretical analysis reveals that this complexity measure offers a substantial improvement in error correction efficiency and robustness, offering a path towards more practical and scalable quantum technologies.

title: Adaptive Probability Field Theory Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive probability field theory optimization algorithm designed to effectively handle complex data sets. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their applicability to relatively simple datasets. This algorithm dynamically adjusts optimization targets based on data probability distributions, enabling it to identify optimal solutions even in challenging scenarios. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of probability fields to guide the optimization process, leading to improved performance and robustness. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, its implementation, and its performance evaluation on a variety of benchmark datasets. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for various applications.

title: Title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Generation via Feedback Loops
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel system for dynamically generating quantum entanglement. Traditional entanglement generation methods are typically static, relying on pre-defined parameters and sequential operations. We propose a dynamic system driven by real-time data analysis, employing a feedback loop to continuously optimize the entanglement rate. This approach offers the potential for significantly enhanced entanglement rates and robustness compared to traditional static methods. title: Borrowing Knowledge Across Tasks: A Critical Survey Review of Transfer Learning and the Pretraining Paradigm
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Transfer Learning and the Pretraining Paradigm in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of transfer learning and pretraining as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Automated Classification of Endometrial Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Hysteroscopy provides direct visualization of the uterine cavity; however, diagnostic outcomes remain highly operator-dependent and subjective. This study aimed to develop an automated deep learning framework based on the ConvNeXt-XLarge architecture, in comparison with an EfficientNetV2 baseline, to objectively classify common uterine pathologies and thereby reduce diagnostic variability. A prospective dataset of 1262 histopathologically confirmed hysteroscopic images was analyzed using an 80:20 training to validation split and a two-stage transfer learning strategy. In addition to the primary multiclass framework, three binary classification models were developed to evaluate pairwise differentiation between the pathologies. The multiclass model achieved an accuracy of 80.5%, a precision of 82.3%, a weighted Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) of 94.8%, and a weighted average precision (AP) of 91.6%. In the binary classification tasks, model 1 (fibroids vs. functional polyps) achieved an accuracy of 96.7% and an AUC of 99.8%; model 2 (fibroids vs. hyperplastic polyps) achieved 87.2% accuracy and an AUC of 87.4%; and model 3 (functional vs. hyperplastic polyps) achieved 92.2% accuracy and an AUC of 99.0%. ConvNeXt-XLarge statistically significantly outperformed EfficientNetV2 in the multiclass task in terms of accuracy and AUC, and in model 2 in terms of accuracy, underscoring the added value of the deeper backbone for this hysteroscopic image classification. Overall, these findings demonstrate that deep learning frameworks can accurately automate the classification of hysteroscopic findings. By providing high-precision analysis, these models offer a robust tool to mitigate diagnostic subjectivity and optimize clinical decision-making.

title: A Channel-Boosted Multi-Agent System with Iterative Consultation for Document Sensitivity Classification
abstract: Organizations in critical national infrastructure sectors must assess heterogeneous documents for sensitivity before routing or storage. Manual assessment is slow, inconsistent, and unscalable. Extending our prior leakage-controlled benchmark, BERT established the top single-encoder baseline (89.14% accuracy, 89.33% F1-score under 5-fold cross-validation on the Strategic 16K corpus). However, transformer baselines suffer from a structural limitation: fixed input length truncation discards evidence beyond the retained window-precisely where sensitive cables tend to be longest. We present Channel-Boosted MAS (CB-MAS) and instantiate it as IC-MAS (Iterative Consultation Multi-Agent System) to solve this without long-context computational costs. A Channel Critic Agent learns document-adaptive trust weights governing Gated Channel Boosting between two first-window encoders, while paired Consultation Agents iteratively exchange belief states to reconcile evidence from the beginning and end of long documents. IC-MAS holds computation constant regardless of document length by reconciling fixed windows in a compact representation space. Ablation studies show critic-controlled Channel Boosting provides the bulk of accuracy gains, while consultation recovers recall without precision collapse. Critic-Controlled Gated Channel Boosting with Max-Pool fusion and Blackboard Adaptive Consultation achieves 90.72% accuracy, 91.23% F1-score, 92.01% sensitive recall, and 90.46% sensitive precision, using about 54% less average computation than a fixed-round baseline. Gains over the single-encoder baseline are statistically significant (McNemar's test, p less than 0.000001; paired t-test). We include LIME/SHAP explainability, multi-agent evaluation, and an honest accounting of limitations.

title: Frontier LLMs are effective batch optimizers: Assessing reasoning models in continuous and discrete settings
abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) have become attractive priors for optimization due to their large-scale pretraining that enables them to navigate a variety of optimization settings. However, the effectiveness of modern reasoning LLMs in batch optimization settings remains underexplored. Here we investigate the performance of the current generation of frontier LLMs as batch optimizers in both continuous and discrete settings. We find that while LLMs are competitive zero-shot batch optimizers for numerical test functions, their performance is brittle compared to classical non-LLM optimization approaches. However, LLM priors are significantly better in semantically rich settings, indicating that their batch optimization behavior is highly effective when navigating and reasoning over the discrete spaces most similar in structure to their pretraining data.

title: Source-Free Class Relearning: Diagnosing Forgetting in Class Unlearning
abstract: Class unlearning aims to remove a model's ability to recognize designated forget classes while preserving performance on retain classes. However, low forget accuracy after unlearning does not necessarily mean the class structure has been erased. Approximate unlearning methods can alter classifier decision boundaries while leaving recoverable structure in the representation. Prior work has shown that forget classes can be recovered, but existing approaches require real forget or retain samples, auxiliary data, or reference checkpoints. We study class relearning in a strictly source-free setting, asking whether a forget class can be recovered through a classifier-head update using only the unlearned model. Our approach rests on a theoretical analysis establishing a sufficient alignment condition under which a single gradient step on a synthetic probe set increases the expected logit margin of the forget class. Building on this, we propose a white-box Source-Free Relearning Audit (SFRA), which generates candidate embeddings in representation space and uses model-guided confidence filtering to construct high-confidence retain probes and low-confidence boundary-adjacent probes that are relabelled as the forget class. Gaussian sampling and Softmax confidence are used by default, while ablations with alternative proposal distributions and uncertainty criteria show that recoverability is not specific to these choices. To quantify recoverability, we introduce the Relearning Score (RS), which jointly measures forget-class recovery and retain-accuracy preservation, and report class-matched $Δ$RS relative to a retrained reference. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet with ResNet-18, ViT-B/16, and Swin-T show that several unlearning methods exhibit substantial source-free recoverability, and that for a subset of methods this recoverability exceeds the matched retrained reference.

title: DevGRU: Depth-Guided Visual Navigation Using a Collision-Aware Recurrent Model
abstract: Existing visual navigation models often aim to develop foundation models that can generalize robot navigation across diverse platforms. However, many of these models are prone to collisions when deployed in complex indoor environments, particularly in structured layouts and narrow passages. To address this problem, we propose a depth image- and point-goal-conditioned navigation system, DevGRU. The proposed system employs an action predictor (AP) that generates collision-aware future trajectories, enabling effective avoidance of immediate obstacles. In conjunction with a collision predictor, the AP further compensates for errors accumulated in the goal pose estimation and proactively mitigates future deviations. To evaluate our method, we conducted experiments across nine different scenes and three state-of-the-art approaches - ViNT, NoMaD, and NavDP - as well as four additional variants of ViNT and NoMaD. In terms of navigation performance, DevGRU significantly outperforms ViNT and NoMaD by a large margin. In addition, the proposed model has a relatively small number of trainable parameters, resulting in the fastest inference time among the baselines, particularly outperforming NavDP by 7x in model size and 17x in inference time.

title: EComAgentBench: Benchmarking Shopping Agents on Long-Horizon Tasks with Distributed Hidden Intent
abstract: As LLM-based shopping agents enter production, existing benchmarks fail to capture how a shopper's requirements arrive: stated implicitly in the query, recorded in a profile, or revealed only when the right question is asked. Benchmarks that expose full intent upfront and grade only the final choice can neither pose this long-horizon challenge nor explain which requirement an agent missed. To address this gap, we introduce EComAgentBench, a benchmark of 662 tasks grounded in real Amazon products and reviews. Each task scatters these requirements across a visible query, a tool-gated profile, and scripted clarification; an agent must uncover hidden intent, verify candidates against attributes and review evidence, and commit to a single product within 100 tool calls. Moreover, typed, source-tagged rubrics grade every task, attributing each failure to a requirement and its source. Construction is automated yet reliable, with every answer fixed in code before any text is generated and every sample validated. Our evaluation of seven models reveals that even the strongest attains only 57.1% overall accuracy, and rubric satisfaction degrades from visible to hidden sources. Overall, we believe EComAgentBench will serve as a reproducible foundation for moving shopping agents from single-query search toward dependable assistance over long horizons.

title: BanffNET, a Deep Learning System for Comprehensive Histological Lesion Quantification in Kidney Transplant Biopsies
authors: LUMC Global Kidney Biopsy Reader Group
abstract: Abstract Accurate, reproducible interpretation of kidney allograft biopsies is critical for the diagnosis of graft injury and for informing prognosis and clinical management. The international Banff classification is a consensus diagnostic system based on semiquantitative histological lesion scoring according to either lesion extent or severity in kidney transplant biopsies. However, pathologist scoring is limited by interobserver variability, constrained scalability, and the inherent nature of the scoring system itself. Here we present BanffNET, a weakly supervised, probabilistic deep learning framework that combines self-supervised feature extraction with a novel Bayesian multiple-instance learning framework to predict (continuously) the full spectrum of Banff lesion scores directly from whole-slide images (WSIs). Using lesion-specific aggregation functions tailored to localized (modeling severity) and diffuse histological lesions (modeling extent), BanffNET generates interpretable, patch-level probability maps and calibrated slide-level scores. BanffNET’s performance was assessed relative to consensus, biological correlates of rejection and clinical outcome, demonstrating superior consistency, transportability and generalization. Trained on 7,533 WSIs from three cohorts, BanffNET demonstrates consistent performance on 12,687 WSIs across five external validation cohorts, matching or surpassing individual expert pathologists across lesion assessments. BanffNET scores align more closely than pathologist Banff scores with molecular profiles of rejection, offering an objective, transparent, biologically grounded framework for computational pathology with relevance beyond kidney transplantation.

title: A Pattern Language for Production LLM Platforms: The pattern relationship graph
abstract: A directed graph of the seventeen patterns in three bands. Infrastructure band: IP-5 gates promotion of IP-1; IP-1 selects from IP-2 and emits IP-4; IP-3 stands apart, bounded by a declared objective. Application band: AP-5 bounds the executor of AP-1; AP-1 is composed as vertices in AP-2; AP-2 is logged as structure by AP-3; AP-3 trains the planner of AP-1, closing the only cycle in the language; AP-4 attaches to nodes of AP-2. Operations band: OP-1 is the route bounded by OP-2; OP-2 and OP-4 are mutually dependent; OP-3 runs inside OP-1; OP-2 bounds the faculties of OP-5; OP-6 supplies evidence for OP-7. Cross-layer edges: AP-5 informs OP-2, and IP-4 with AP-3 are reused as the metering path by OP-6. The economic chain runs IP-1 to IP-4 to OP-6 to OP-7 across the full height of the stack. This figure is Figure 4 of A Pattern Language for Production LLM Platforms, version 1.1, deposited at Zenodo. title: Selective Quantum Intervention for Network Intrusion Detection: Benefit–Risk Routing, Safe Abstention, and Finite-Shot Robustness
abstract: This repository provides the reproducibility package for a selective quantum intervention framework for network intrusion detection. The proposed approach treats quantum inference as a conditional computational resource rather than a universal replacement for classical classification. A strong classical intrusion detection model remains the default decision mechanism, while a benefit–risk routing strategy selectively authorizes quantum intervention for samples where correction benefit is predicted to outweigh the risk of breaking an otherwise correct classical prediction. The principal S-QIDS architecture combines boundary eligibility, break-risk rejection, correction-benefit estimation, a fixed fidelity-based quantum classifier, and safe override or abstention. Quantum Utilization Rate (QUR) and Net Quantum Benefit Rate (NQBR) are used to quantify resource utilization and the net value of selective intervention. The package contains code, experimental configurations, evaluation procedures, and supporting results for leakage-controlled repeated-seed validation, matched-utilization controls, cross-dataset evaluation, frozen-state reproduction, and repeated finite-shot statistical robustness analysis. The principal UNSW-NB15 evaluation demonstrates constrained positive selective routing utility while invoking the quantum component for only a small fraction of test samples. Cross-dataset experiments also examine safe abstention when the frozen router does not identify sufficiently reliable intervention opportunities. Repeated finite-shot experiments assess statistical stability of the frozen selective intervention under measurement randomness and controlled generic state-level depolarizing perturbations. The results should not be interpreted as evidence of universal quantum advantage, physical quantum-hardware robustness, or guaranteed computational speedup. They instead provide evidence for selective, conditional, and complementary quantum utility under the experimental protocols documented in this repository.

title: 基于记忆网络的量子计算的参数优化
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential for solving complex problems intractable for classical computers. However, the development of efficient quantum algorithms relies heavily on the precise optimization of quantum parameters. This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum parameter optimization utilizing a dynamically learning quantum memory network. We propose a system where quantum states are represented as a memory network, allowing the network to learn and adapt to the system's environment during the optimization process. This dynamic learning mechanism promises to automate the parameter adjustment, leading to improved quantum algorithm performance. The core mechanism of this research is the implementation of a quantum memory network that learns and dynamically adjusts parameters based on observed quantum states. This offers a fundamentally different paradigm compared to traditional parameter optimization methods. The potential benefits include enhanced algorithm performance, reduced computational cost, and a more adaptable system capable of addressing complex quantum problems. We present a preliminary implementation of this system, demonstrating its capabilities through a simplified quantum circuit optimization task.

title: Title: Dynamical Quantum Error Correction with Adaptive Thresholds
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, but the inherent fragility of quantum information necessitates robust error correction techniques. Current methods often rely on meticulous calibration procedures, limiting their applicability and hindering scalability. This paper presents a novel dynamical quantum error correction scheme leveraging adaptive thresholding, designed to mitigate the impact of system noise through a continuous feedback loop. We detail the proposed mechanism, its underlying mathematical principles, and a comprehensive evaluation of its performance against established techniques. The core claim highlights the significant improvement in resilience to noise, offering a more adaptable and robust strategy for quantum error correction.

title: 基于图的变量空间优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel variable space optimization algorithm based on graph representation. Traditional variable space optimization methods often focus on optimizing variable distributions, while graph structures offer a powerful mechanism for improving numerical computation efficiency. We propose a method that transforms the variable space into a graph, leveraging the graph's inherent structure to guide optimization. This approach allows for a more flexible and robust optimization process compared to traditional methods. The algorithm demonstrates improved performance in a series of benchmark problems, highlighting its potential for enhancing numerical computation.

title: Adaptive Neural Architecture Search with Evolutionary Strategies and Bayesian Uncertainty
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has emerged as a powerful technique for automating the design of neural networks, offering the potential to discover architectures that outperform human-designed models. However, current NAS methods often suffer from limited exploration of the vast architecture space, leading to suboptimal solutions. This work addresses this challenge by integrating Evolutionary Strategies (ES) with Bayesian Uncertainty Estimation. The core idea is to leverage ES for efficient exploration while simultaneously incorporating Bayesian methods to quantify and manage the uncertainty associated with each proposed architecture. This adaptive approach allows the algorithm to intelligently prioritize architectures with high potential and avoid those with high uncertainty, resulting in a more robust and efficient NAS process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this combined approach through theoretical analysis and a detailed explanation of the algorithm's components. The resulting adaptive architecture search method significantly improves the quality and convergence speed of NAS, providing a promising direction for future research in automated neural architecture design.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Optimization with Adaptive Query Strategies
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Bayesian Optimization (BO) that leverages quantum computation to significantly accelerate the optimization process. The core idea is to employ a quantum circuit to estimate the gradient of the objective function, providing a richer and potentially more accurate signal for the classical Bayesian optimizer. Crucially, the algorithm incorporates adaptive query strategies, dynamically adjusting its exploration based on the observed interference effects within the quantum circuit. This synergy between classical Bayesian inference and quantum gradient estimation promises enhanced exploration and faster convergence compared to traditional BO methods. We detail the architecture of the proposed algorithm, outlining the quantum circuit design, the Bayesian optimization framework, and the adaptive query strategy. The theoretical analysis suggests a potential improvement in the exploration efficiency, particularly in high-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm's adaptability allows it to overcome challenges often encountered in BO, such as the "curse of dimensionality," leading to improved performance across a range of optimization problems. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through a conceptual framework and analytical discussion, highlighting the key components and their interactions.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A Comparative Analysis Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Field-Adaptive Probability Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probability modeling, termed Field-Adaptive Probability Models (FAPMs), which dynamically adjusts model parameters and assumptions based on data distribution. The core innovation lies in integrating a probabilistic model with a self-adjusting mechanism, enabling the model to effectively mitigate model generalization errors and capture complex data characteristics. We demonstrate the efficacy of FAPMs through extensive simulations and experimental analysis, showcasing improved predictive accuracy compared to traditional models in a range of datasets. The paper highlights the advantages of this approach in scenarios with evolving data distributions.

title: Formal Language-Based Program Verification Tools
abstract: This paper explores the development and application of program verification tools grounded in formal languages. The core idea revolves around leveraging the precision and rigor of formal systems, such as logic and linear boolean algebra, to rigorously analyze and verify the correctness and security properties of software. Current program verification techniques often rely on finite state machines or state space representations, which can be limiting in terms of expressiveness and scalability. This research proposes a shift towards a more comprehensive approach by directly translating programs into formal language representations, enabling the utilization of established formal verification methodologies like model checking and theorem proving. The presented framework aims to provide a robust and reliable method for ensuring software quality, particularly in safety-critical applications where correctness is paramount. The paper details the theoretical foundations, key components, and potential benefits of this approach, highlighting its advantages over existing state-based verification techniques.

title: Quantum Computing Resource Allocation and Scheduling Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to resource allocation and scheduling within quantum computing environments. Recognizing the inherent scarcity and unique characteristics of quantum resources, such as qubits and quantum gates, we propose a dynamic algorithm designed to optimize resource utilization and consequently enhance computational efficiency. The core of the algorithm lies in a mechanism that intelligently balances the demands of diverse quantum computing tasks. We formalize this approach using mathematical notation, detailing the key components including task prioritization, qubit assignment, gate scheduling, and dynamic adjustment based on real-time system metrics. The proposed algorithm addresses limitations within existing static scheduling methods, offering improved performance in complex quantum workflows. The design incorporates a queuing theory-inspired model to manage task flow and a stochastic optimization technique for adaptive resource allocation. Simulation results (presented conceptually here) demonstrate the algorithm's potential to significantly improve quantum computing performance compared to traditional approaches. Further research will focus on formal verification and optimization for specific quantum computing architectures.

title: Neural Code Interpreter: Decoding Program Execution in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to computation by leveraging the inherent coding capabilities of neural networks. We introduce the concept of a "Neural Code Interpreter" (NCI), which utilizes the patterns of neural activity within a network to dynamically interpret and execute traditional program instructions. The core idea is to map program instructions to specific activation patterns within a neural network, effectively transforming the network into a programmable interpreter. This shifts the paradigm from static, pre-defined instructions to a dynamic, adaptive execution model. We outline the theoretical framework, detail the mapping process, and explore the potential implications of this approach, highlighting its ability to achieve dynamic execution of traditional programs through neural network activity. The NCI presents a fundamentally different computational model, opening possibilities for novel algorithms and architectures. ---
